newsitem.title: USA: Grand Casinos agrees to Stratosphere restructuring.
newsitem.headline: Grand Casinos agrees to Stratosphere restructuring.

text.p: Grand Casinos Inc said Monday it agreed to a restructuring plan for Stratosphere Corp under which Grand Casinos will convert $50 million due from Stratosphere into 40 percent of the common stock of Stratosphere upon completion of the plan.
A consensual Chapter 11 bankruptcy reorganization of Stratosphere is expected to be presented to Federal Bankruptcy Court in Nevada later this month.
As of October 1, Grand Casinos held a 42 percent stake in Stratosphere, a casino and hotel property company.

Grand Casinos said 60 percent of the post-reorganization common stock ownership of Stratosphere will be sold through a rights offering to all existing holders of Stratosphere, including Grand Casinos. The rights offering will generate net proceeds of about $75 million.

As part of the restructuring plan, Grand Casinos said it agreed to buy its pro rata share of the rights offering (about 42 percent) for about $31.9 million. It also will provide a standby commitment to buy any unsubscribed portion of the rights offering not exercised by other Stratosphere shareholders.
Existing Stratosphere shares will be canceled and shareholders will receive a transferable right to buy one share of common stock in the reorganized Stratosphere at $1.31 a share.

Each purchaser of a share through the rights offering, other than those subscribed by Grand Casinos as its pro rata portion, also will receive a three-year warrant to purchase one-half share of common stock at $3 per full share.

The rights offering will result in issuance of 58 million shares of Stratosphere common stock. Upon completion of the reorganization and rights offering, Stratosphere will have about 96.7 million shares of common stock outstanding and warrants outstanding to purchase another roughly 17 million shares of common stock at $3 a share.
Grand Casinos owns and operates three casino hotel resorts in Mississippi, manages two land-based casinos in Louisiana and manages two casino hotel resorts in Minnesota.
